prompt-v2 (frozen C2).rationale: The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.97–1.0 from 6 h onward. A plateau like that could be reader saturation hiding continued growth, so I diluted the retained aliquots to test it. At 18 h, the 10x dilution read 0.106 (×10 = 1.06) and the 30x dilution read 0.032 (×30 = 0.95). At 12 h, the 10x dilution read 0.099 (×10 = 0.99). All the diluted readings, scaled back up, come to about 1.0, which matches the undiluted ~0.97. If the reader were saturating, the scaled-up diluted values would be well above the undiluted ones. The small differences between the scaled values (0.95–1.06) are within replicate noise. The plateau is therefore real stationary phase at OD ~1, and the undiluted readings are accurate.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.76 from 5 h onward, which looks like reader saturation. The 18 h aliquot read 0.264 at 10-fold dilution (two replicates, 0.261 and 0.267) and 0.090 at 30-fold dilution. Scaled back, those give about 2.64 and 2.71. The two dilutions agree, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The true OD at 18 h is therefore about 2.7, roughly 3.5 times the undiluted reading of 0.75.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.964 undiluted. At 10x dilution (n=2) it read 0.0991 and 0.0972, which is about 0.98 once multiplied back. At 3x dilution (n=1) it read 0.3267, which is also about 0.98. The dilution-corrected values agree with the undiluted reading to within about 2%. The reader therefore responds proportionally up to about 1.0, and the plateau at roughly 0.95 reflects stationary phase, not detector saturation. Biomass is not higher than the undiluted readings indicate.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.3 from 7 h onward, which looks like the reader saturating. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to check. At 10x the readings were 0.4773 and 0.478, which scale to about 4.78. At 40x the single reading was 0.122, which scales to about 4.9. Both dilutions agree on a value near 4.8–4.9, well above the undiluted 1.31. The culture is still growing or is at a much higher density than the plateau shows, and the undiluted reading under-reports it.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.5 from 5 h onward. I diluted the retained 18 h aliquot to test whether the reader was saturating. At 10x, the two replicates read 0.0513 and 0.0506, which is about 0.509 after correcting for dilution. At 2x, one replicate read 0.244, which is about 0.488 after correcting. Both match the undiluted 18 h reading of 0.492. The response is linear across the dilution range, so there is no sign of saturation or other nonlinearity. The plateau reflects stationary phase, and the biomass is at the level the undiluted readings indicate.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.52 from 5 h onward, right after exponential growth. That flat ceiling suggests the reader is saturating. The 18 h aliquot supports this. At 10x dilution it read 0.193 (two replicates, 0.1934 and 0.1928), which corresponds to about 1.93. At 25x it read 0.0734, or about 1.84. At 50x it read 0.0441, or about 2.2. If the 0.52 were the true OD, a 10x dilution would read about 0.05, not 0.19. The diluted readings agree with each other at roughly 1.9–2.0, which is about 3.7 times the undiluted reading. The undiluted plateau therefore reflects reader saturation, not a true stationary biomass.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.443 undiluted. At 4-fold dilution the mean was 0.1046, which is 0.418 after correcting for dilution. At 10-fold dilution the mean was 0.0464, which is 0.464 after correcting. These corrected values agree with the undiluted reading within replicate scatter (about ±0.03). If the reader were saturating at OD ~0.44, the diluted samples would read clearly higher than 0.44 after correction, and they do not. The plateau from 6 h onward therefore reflects real stationary phase, and the undiluted readings are proportional to biomass.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 2.0 from 8 h onward, after exponential growth up to 7 h. That looks like the reader saturating, not a real stationary phase. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to test this. A 10x dilution read 0.727 (two replicates, 0.724 and 0.729), which is about 7.3 undiluted. A 25x dilution read 0.298, which is about 7.45 undiluted. These two corrected values agree with each other and are about 3.7 times the undiluted reading of 2.0. So the reader is non-linear at high density, and the true OD at 18 h is about 7.5.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.22 from 6 h onward. If the reader were saturating, diluted aliquots would read much higher than the undiluted value once the dilution factor was applied. The 18 h aliquot did not do this. The dilution-corrected values were 1.35 (10x, n=2), 1.26 (20x, n=2) and 1.17 (40x, n=1), against 1.209 undiluted. They have no consistent upward trend with dilution and the mean is only about 3% above the undiluted reading, which is within noise. The 6 h control (10x gave 1.213 against 1.236 undiluted) shows the reader is linear at this OD. The plateau therefore looks like genuine stationary phase, and the biomass is as read.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.85 from 9 h onward, and the exponential rise (roughly doubling per hour) stops abruptly at 8–9 h. The 18 h aliquot read at 10-fold dilution gave 0.661 and 0.643. That corresponds to about 6.5 OD undiluted, against 1.91 read undiluted. A 25-fold dilution of the same aliquot gave 0.261, which also corresponds to about 6.5 OD. Two different dilutions give the same back-calculated value, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The flat undiluted readings are therefore a saturated reader response, not a stationary phase at OD 1.9. The true late biomass is about 3.4 times higher than the undiluted readings indicate.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.73 from 7 h to 18 h. If the reader were saturating, diluted aliquots would read well above the undiluted value once scaled back up. I tested the 18 h aliquot at three dilutions. The 3x dilution read 0.2435, or 0.73 scaled. The 10x dilution read 0.0766, or 0.77 scaled (replicates 0.0763 and 0.077). The 30x dilution read 0.0253, or 0.76 scaled (replicates 0.0229 and 0.0277, noisier). All three fall within about 5% of the undiluted 0.73. The slight excess is small and consistent with noise or minor non-linearity, so the plateau reflects real stationary phase and the biomass is at the level the undiluted readings indicate.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 0.5 from 4 h onward. The 18 h aliquot read 0.193 at 10x dilution (two replicates, 0.189 and 0.198), which scales to about 1.9. A 50x dilution read 0.033, which scales to about 1.65, but it is near the low end of the reader's range and is noisier. Both are far above the undiluted 0.506, so the reader is saturating and the plateau is an artefact. The 4 h aliquot also read higher when diluted (0.0594 at 10x, scaling to 0.59, against 0.48 undiluted), so saturation starts at about 0.5. The true late biomass is therefore about 1.7–2 OD units, not about 0.5.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.42 from 6 h onward, which could mean either stationary phase or reader saturation. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to test this. A 10x dilution read 0.0432 (0.0472 and 0.0392), which scales to 0.43. A 3x dilution read 0.154 (0.160 and 0.148), which scales to 0.46. Both scaled values are close to the undiluted 0.42, within the roughly ±0.005 read noise multiplied by the dilution factor. If the reader were saturating, the diluted samples would scale to well above 0.42, for example 0.6 or more. They do not, so the plateau looks like genuine stationary phase and the undiluted readings are about right.

The undiluted readings sit at a flat plateau of about 1.1 from 6 h to 18 h, which suggests the reader is saturating. I diluted the 18 h aliquot 10-fold and read 0.5226 (replicates 0.5275 and 0.5177), which corresponds to about 5.2 OD. A 25-fold dilution read 0.2078, which corresponds to about 5.2 OD again. Two different dilutions agree, so the dilute readings are in the proportional range. The true late OD is therefore about 5.2, roughly 4–5 times the undiluted reading of about 1.1.

I diluted the 18 h aliquot and scaled each reading back up by its dilution factor. The undiluted reading was 1.553. The 2-fold dilution read 0.8026, which scales to 1.605. The 10-fold dilution read 0.1681 and 0.1627, which scales to about 1.65. The 20-fold dilution read 0.0782, which scales to 1.564. All four estimates agree within about 6%. If the reader were saturating at about 1.6, the diluted samples would scale up to clearly higher values, and they do not. The plateau from about 7 h onward therefore reflects real stationary phase, not detector saturation. The small excess in the 10-fold dilution is within replicate and pipetting noise and shows no trend with dilution.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.93–0.95 from 5 h to 18 h. This flat ceiling after steep exponential growth looks like reader saturation, not a true stationary phase. I diluted the retained 18 h aliquot to test this. At 10-fold dilution it read 0.361 (replicates 0.3616 and 0.3608), which scales to about 3.6. At 40-fold dilution it read 0.0816, which scales to about 3.3. Both are far above the undiluted 0.955. The two scaled values are close but not identical. The 10-fold value is slightly higher, which suggests some residual nonlinearity at 0.36. The true OD at 18 h is therefore about 3.3–3.6, roughly 3.5 times the undiluted reading.

The 18 h aliquot was read at three dilutions. The values below are the reading multiplied back by the dilution factor. All are consistent with the undiluted reading of 1.29, so the plateau is real stationary phase and not detector saturation.

- 3x: 0.439, which gives about 1.32.
- 10x: 0.125, which gives about 1.25.
- 40x: 0.037, which gives about 1.48. This is within the noise, since a reading error of about 0.005 becomes about 0.2 after multiplying by 40.

If the reader were saturating, the diluted readings would scale back to values clearly above 1.3. They do not.

The undiluted readings stay flat at about 0.90–0.95 from 6 h to 18 h, after roughly doubling every hour up to 5 h. That flat line looks like the reader saturating rather than growth stopping. I diluted the 18 h aliquot and got 0.334 at 10-fold (mean of 3 replicates: 0.323, 0.334, 0.346) and 0.0815 at 40-fold (1 replicate). Scaled back up, these give about 3.34 and 3.26. The two dilutions agree, so the signal is linear in that range. The true 18 h OD is therefore about 3.3, roughly 3.6 times the undiluted reading of 0.91, so the undiluted readings underestimate the biomass.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.48 from 5 h onward, which could mean the reader was saturating. I diluted the 18 h aliquot and rescaled the readings by the dilution factor. If the reader were saturating, these would come out higher than the undiluted reading.

| Dilution | Reading(s) | Rescaled OD |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (undiluted) | 0.4885 | 0.489 |
| 2 (2 replicates) | 0.245, 0.244 | 0.489 |
| 3 (1 replicate, 2 runs) | 0.176 and 0.166 | 0.528 and 0.498 |
| 10 (2 replicates) | 0.049, 0.047 | 0.481 |

The rescaled values stay between 0.48 and 0.53 and do not rise with dilution. The first 3x reading (0.528) was somewhat high, but a repeat gave 0.498, so I treat it as noise. The plateau therefore looks like a real stationary phase at an OD of about 0.49, and the undiluted readings are not under-reporting biomass.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.65 from 7 h onward, right after steep exponential growth. That looks like reader saturation rather than a true stationary phase. The 18 h aliquot read 0.251 at 10x dilution, which corresponds to about 2.5 OD. At 40x dilution it read 0.0552, which corresponds to about 2.2 OD. Both are roughly 3.5-4 times the undiluted reading of 0.644. The 10x value is slightly higher than the 40x value, so some nonlinearity probably remains at 0.25. The best estimate of true biomass is therefore about 2.2-2.5 OD, with the 40x reading the less saturated and so the more reliable.

The 18 h aliquot was read at three dilutions. At 10x the two replicates were 0.1185 and 0.1217, which scales to about 1.20. At 3x the reading was 0.4024, which scales to about 1.21. At 30x the reading was 0.039, which scales to about 1.17 and is noisier because the signal is low. The undiluted reading was 1.161. The dilution-corrected values are within about 3-4% of the undiluted reading and show no trend with dilution. If the reader were saturating, the corrected values would be well above the undiluted reading and would rise with dilution. The plateau at about 1.16 from 8 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase and not a reader ceiling. A very small compression of about 3% at the top of the range is possible but is not meaningful.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.2 from 7 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. Diluting the 18 h aliquot 10-fold gave 0.482 (replicates 0.479 and 0.484), which corresponds to about 4.8 OD undiluted. A 20-fold dilution gave 0.232, which corresponds to about 4.6 OD. The two dilutions roughly agree, and both are about 4 times the undiluted reading of 1.2. The reader is linear at lower density: the 6 h aliquot read 0.557 undiluted and 0.277 at 2-fold dilution, as expected. The reader therefore compresses high-density readings, and true late biomass is about 4.6–4.8 OD, well above what the undiluted readings show.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.96 from 6 h onward, which could mean either stationary phase or detector saturation. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to check. At 10x, the two reads were 0.094 and 0.0967 (mean 0.0953), which is 0.953 after multiplying back. At 3x, the single read was 0.3127, which is 0.938 after multiplying back. Both back-calculated values match the undiluted reading of 0.9625. If the reader had been saturating, the diluted samples would have given higher back-calculated values. They did not, so the response is linear in this range and the plateau is real stationary-phase biomass.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.92–0.97 from 6 h to 18 h, which looks like reader saturation or nonlinearity. The retained 18 h aliquot confirms this. Diluted 10-fold, it read 0.481 and 0.475, which corrects to about 4.78. Diluted 40-fold, it read 0.114, which corrects to about 4.57. Both dilutions give a corrected OD of roughly 4.6–4.8, about 5 times the undiluted reading of 0.92. The two dilutions agree closely, and the diluted readings fall within the range where the reader responds proportionally. So the true biomass over the final hours is well above what the undiluted readings indicate.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.53 from 5 h onward. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to check whether that plateau was a reader ceiling. The dilution-corrected values (reading × dilution) were 0.536 at 3×, 0.575 at 10× (2 replicates), 0.468 at 20× and 0.62 at 30× (2 replicates). All of these are close to the undiluted 0.531. They do not rise steadily with dilution, which a saturating reader would produce. The spread looks like noise, which is larger at the very low raw readings of 0.02. The plateau therefore looks like genuine stationary phase, and biomass is at the level the undiluted readings indicate.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.68 from 7 h onward. That is consistent with the reader saturating rather than growth stopping. The 18 h aliquot read 0.33 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.337 and 0.324), which scales to about 3.3. At 40x it read 0.080, which scales to about 3.2. The two dilutions agree with each other and are about 5 times the undiluted reading of 0.67. So the undiluted reader is strongly non-linear at high density and the true late biomass is about 3.3 OD-equivalent.

The undiluted reading plateaus at about 0.60-0.65 from 5 h to 18 h. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to test whether that plateau is reader saturation. The 3x dilution read 0.2031, which scales to 0.609. The 10x dilution read 0.0631 and 0.0673, which scale to 0.63-0.67. The undiluted reading was 0.605. Diluted readings scale back to roughly the undiluted value, so the reader responds proportionally in this range and does not hide extra biomass. The 10x result is about 8% higher than the undiluted reading, which is small and could be noise. The plateau therefore looks like real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.1 from 9 h onward. The 18 h aliquot read 0.520 at 10x dilution (n=2), which is about 5.2 after correcting for dilution. At 40x it read 0.1315 (n=2), which is about 5.26. The two dilutions agree with each other, and both are in the range where the reader responds linearly. They are about 4.7 times higher than the undiluted reading of 1.10. The plateau therefore reflects reader saturation, not stationary phase at that density. The true late-phase biomass is about 5.2 OD-equivalent.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.34 from 7 h onward. The 18 h aliquot read at several dilutions gives a higher dilution-corrected OD as the dilution increases: undiluted 1.34, ×4 gives 1.40, ×10 gives 1.47 (two replicates, 0.1451 and 0.1484), and ×40 gives 1.52 (two replicates, 0.0385 and 0.0375). The readings are not proportional to concentration. The plate reader saturates at high density, so the plateau is partly an artefact. The corrected values are still rising at the highest dilution, so the true OD is probably about 1.5 or a little more. That is roughly 10–15% above the undiluted reading. The effect is modest, but the trend is consistent and larger than the replicate scatter.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.65 from 5 h onward. The 18 h aliquot read 0.3015 at 10x dilution (about 3.0 undiluted-equivalent) and 0.0592 at 50x dilution (about 2.96). The two dilutions agree with each other and are about 4.5 times the undiluted reading. That points to reader saturation or non-linearity at high density, so the plateau is an artefact and the biomass is higher than the undiluted readings indicate. I did not run a separate linearity check at an earlier time point.

prompt-v2-minimal.rationale: The 18 h aliquot gave dilution-corrected ODs of about 1.03 (3x), 1.06 (10x), 0.95 (20x) and 0.72 (100x). The 100x reading is near the noise floor. Undiluted reading was 0.97. The dilution-corrected values scatter around 1.0 and do not rise with dilution, so there is no sign of detector saturation. The plateau is a real stationary phase at OD about 1.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.76 from 5 h onward. A 10-fold dilution of the 18 h aliquot read 0.264 (replicates 0.261 and 0.267), which corresponds to an OD of about 2.6, not 0.75. That is a clear non-linear, saturating response of the undiluted reading. The 5 h aliquot diluted 10-fold read 0.082, or about 0.82 corrected, against 0.725 undiluted. This shows the compression starting at that point. The plateau therefore reflects the reading ceiling and not stationary phase at 0.76, so the late biomass is higher than the readings indicate.

Diluted re-reads match undiluted readings. At 18 h, 10x dilution gave 0.098, which is 0.98 corrected. At 12 h, 100x dilution gave 0.0095, which is 0.95 corrected. There is no sign of saturation or a nonlinear detector response, so the plateau at about 0.95 is real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.3 from 7 h onward, which looks like the reader saturating. At 18 h, a 10-fold dilution read 0.478 (replicates 0.4773 and 0.478), which corresponds to OD of about 4.78. A 40-fold dilution read 0.122, which corresponds to about 4.88. The two dilutions agree, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The true OD at 18 h is about 4.8, which is well above the 1.3 read undiluted.

The 18 h aliquot diluted 10-fold read 0.0509 in two replicates (0.0513 and 0.0506). Multiplied back, that is about 0.51, which matches the undiluted reading of 0.492. If the plateau at about 0.5 were detector saturation, the diluted sample would have read well above 0.05. It did not, so the stationary plateau is real.

The undiluted readings rise exponentially and then sit flat at about 0.52 from hour 5 onward, which suggests the reader is saturating. The 18 h aliquot diluted 10-fold read 0.193 in both replicates (0.1934 and 0.1928). That corresponds to an OD of about 1.93, well above the undiluted 0.52. A real plateau would give about 0.05 after a 10-fold dilution. The late biomass is therefore higher than the undiluted readings indicate.

At 18 h the diluted reads, scaled back up, match the undiluted reading (about 0.44). The 2x dilution gave 0.228, which is 0.457 after scaling. The 10x dilution gave 0.039, which is 0.39 after scaling, and this read is noisy at low signal. The reading does not rise as the sample is diluted, so there is no sign of saturation or non-linearity. The plateau at about 0.43 is therefore real stationary phase.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 2.0 from 8 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. The 18 h aliquot read 0.727 at 10x dilution (about 7.3 OD) and 0.372 at 20x dilution (about 7.4 OD). That is roughly 3.7 times the undiluted reading, and the two dilutions agree. The true late OD is about 7.4.

Diluted re-reads of the 18 h aliquot, scaled back by the dilution factor, gave 1.27 (5x), 1.35 (10x, two replicates), 1.19 (30x) and 0.88 (100x). The 100x value is near the noise floor. Undiluted reading was 1.21. The scaled values scatter around 1.2–1.3 with no trend upward as dilution increases, so there is no sign of detector saturation. A 10x dilution of the 5 h aliquot gave 0.898 scaled, against 0.935 undiluted, so dilution scales linearly. The plateau at about 1.2 looks like real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.85 from 9 h onward. That is consistent with detector saturation. At 18 h, a 10x dilution read 0.652, which corresponds to about 6.5 OD. A 40x dilution read 0.163, which corresponds to about 6.5 OD. The two dilutions agree, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The true OD at 18 h is therefore about 3.5 times the undiluted reading.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.728 undiluted. After correcting for dilution, it read 0.744 at 3x (0.248) and 0.766 at 10x (0.0766). These values agree within noise, so the readings are linear. There is no sign of detector saturation or of a hidden higher biomass. The plateau at about 0.73–0.76 appears to be real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.5 from 4 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. The 18 h aliquot read 0.193 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.189 and 0.198) and 0.065 at 30x dilution. Both correct to about 1.9–1.95 OD, so the two dilutions agree. That is about 4 times the undiluted reading of 0.5.

The culture plateaus at an OD of about 0.42 from 6 h onward. Diluted reads scale back to the undiluted value. At 18 h, a 10x dilution read 0.0432, which gives 0.43 against 0.42 undiluted. At 12 h, a 4x dilution read 0.117, which gives 0.47 against 0.43 undiluted. The 12 h value is slightly higher, but replicate scatter of about 0.005 per read, scaled by 4, covers the difference. A saturated or non-linear reading would give a clearly higher diluted OD, and that did not appear. The plateau therefore looks like genuine stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.1 from 6 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. The 18 h aliquot read 0.5226 at 10x dilution, which corresponds to about 5.2 undiluted. A 40x dilution read 0.1293, which corresponds to about 5.17 undiluted. The two dilutions agree, so the true OD at 18 h is about 5.2, well above the 1.1 reading.

The readings plateau at about 1.6 from 7 h onward. If the plateau were detector saturation, diluted reads scaled back up would exceed the undiluted reading. At 18 h the undiluted reading was 1.55. The 10x dilution gave 0.165, which scales to 1.65. The 100x dilution gave 0.0134, which scales to 1.34. Neither is meaningfully above the undiluted value, and the 100x read is lower, probably because of noise or offset at such a low OD. This is consistent with a true stationary phase at an OD of about 1.6.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.93–0.95 from 5 h onward. That looks like detector saturation. At 18 h, the 10-fold diluted sample read 0.361 (two replicates, 0.3616 and 0.3608), which corresponds to an OD of about 3.6. The 25-fold diluted sample read 0.134, which corresponds to about 3.4. Both are far above the undiluted 0.95. The 10-fold value is slightly higher than the 25-fold value, so the 10-fold reading may have been slightly non-linear. The true OD at 18 h is therefore about 3.4–3.6, well above the plateau reading.

The 18 h aliquot was read at dilution factors 3, 10 and 30. Multiplying each reading by its dilution factor gives about 1.41, 1.25 and 1.29. These agree with the undiluted reading of 1.29, so the signal is linear. If the plateau came from detector saturation, the diluted readings would scale up to well above 1.3. They don't, so the stationary plateau is real biomass.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 0.9 from 6 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. The 18 h aliquot diluted 10x read 0.328 (×10 = 3.28). Diluted 40x it read 0.0815 (×40 = 3.26). The two dilutions agree, so the dilution-corrected OD is about 3.3, well above the 0.9 read undiluted.

Diluted retained aliquots scale linearly with dilution. At 18 h, 10-fold dilution gave 0.048, which is 0.48 after correction. At 16 h, 2-fold dilution gave 0.2445, which is 0.489 after correction. At 14 h, 3-fold dilution gave 0.176, which is 0.528 after correction, about 10% above the undiluted reading. That single read is probably noise, since the other two agree with the undiluted plateau of about 0.48. There is no sign of saturation or nonlinearity, so the plateau is real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.65 from 7 h onward. This follows exponential growth and is abrupt, which suggests the reading is saturating. At 18 h the 10-fold dilution read 0.251, which corresponds to about 2.5 OD. The 30-fold dilution read 0.0754, which corresponds to about 2.26 OD. Both are far above the undiluted 0.64. The 10-fold value is a little higher than the 30-fold value, so some nonlinearity probably remains at 0.25. The true OD at 18 h is therefore roughly 2.3 to 2.6.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.120 at a 10-fold dilution (replicates 0.1185 and 0.1217). That corrects to about 1.20, which matches the undiluted reading of 1.16. If the plateau were detector saturation, the diluted sample would have read well above 0.116. The plateau from 8 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 1.2 from 7 h onward, which looks like a ceiling. Diluting the 18 h aliquot 10-fold read 0.482, which is about 4.8 OD after correcting for dilution. Diluting it 40-fold read 0.123, which is about 4.9 OD. The two corrected values agree with each other and are about 4 times the undiluted reading. The plateau is therefore signal saturation, not a stationary phase at OD 1.2.

The OD plateaus at about 0.96 from 6 h onward. That could be detector saturation, but a 10-fold dilution of the 18 h aliquot read 0.0953 (replicates 0.094 and 0.0967). That is 0.953 once multiplied back, which matches the undiluted reading of 0.9625. The response is linear, so the plateau is a real stationary phase and not saturation.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 0.95 from 6 h onward, which suggests the reader is saturating. The 18 h aliquot diluted 10-fold read 0.478 (replicates 0.481 and 0.475). That corresponds to about 4.8 OD undiluted, roughly 5 times the undiluted reading of 0.92. The culture is still well above the plateau value, so biomass is higher than the readings indicate.

At 18 h, the diluted aliquots scale back to about the undiluted reading of 0.53. Dilutions of 5×, 10× and 30× give 0.52, 0.575 and 0.62 after correcting for dilution. If the plateau were caused by detector saturation, the diluted readings would scale back to much higher values. The 5 h aliquot read at 10× gives 0.524, which matches its undiluted reading of 0.529. This indicates the reader is linear in this range. The 30× result is noisy (0.52 and 0.72 from the two replicates), and the small upward drift across the dilutions is within that noise. The plateau reflects stationary phase.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 0.67–0.70 from 7 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. The 18 h aliquot read at 10× dilution gave 0.33, or about 3.3 OD after correcting for dilution. At 40× it gave 0.080, or about 3.2 OD. Both dilutions agree with each other and are about 5 times the undiluted reading of 0.67, so the plateau is a measurement ceiling and the culture is still well above what the undiluted readings show.

The 18 h aliquot was diluted 10-fold and read 0.0652 (replicates 0.0631 and 0.0673). That scales to about 0.65, which matches the undiluted reading of 0.605. If the plateau were caused by detector saturation, the diluted reading would have been much higher. The plateau at about 0.6 from 5 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.1 from 9 h onward. Diluted readings of the 18 h aliquot do not match that plateau. At 10x dilution the mean was 0.520, which gives 5.2 OD after correcting for dilution. At 40x dilution the reading was 0.128, which gives 5.13 OD. The two dilutions agree with each other, so the diluted reads are in the linear range. The undiluted plateau is therefore signal saturation, and the true late biomass is about 5 times the reading.

The undiluted readings are flat at about 1.34 from 7 h to 18 h, which looks like a plateau. I diluted the 18 h aliquot and scaled the readings back up. These were the results:
- 10x dilution: 0.1467 mean, which scales to about 1.47.
- 20x dilution: 0.0737 mean, which scales to about 1.47.
- 50x dilution: 0.0308 mean, which scales to about 1.54. This one is noisier because the signal is so low.

All three dilutions agree with each other at about 1.47–1.54. That is consistently higher than the undiluted reading of about 1.34, so the undiluted reading is compressed at high OD. The plateau therefore understates the late biomass by roughly 10%. The size of the gap is modest, which is why I put the probability at 0.85 and not higher.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.65 from hour 5 onward. Diluted readings of the 18 h aliquot are much higher once scaled back. At 10-fold dilution the reading was 0.30 (two replicates), which gives about 3.0. At 40-fold dilution it was 0.077, which gives about 3.1. The two dilutions agree, so the signal is linear when diluted. The 0.65 plateau is therefore detector saturation, and the real OD is about 3 at 18 h.

prompt-v2-noceiling.rationale: The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.97-1.0 from 6 h onward. I tested whether that plateau was reader saturation by diluting the 18 h aliquot. Scaled back by the dilution factor, the results were: 10x gave 0.1064, or about 1.06 (replicates 0.1071 and 0.1056); 3x gave 0.327, or about 0.98; 50x gave 0.0186, or about 0.93 (noisy, replicates 0.0225 and 0.0148). All sit within about 10% of the undiluted 0.97. If the reader were saturating or hiding biomass, the diluted readings scaled up would be well above the undiluted value, and they are not. The culture therefore appears to have a true stationary plateau at OD of roughly 1.0, with at most slight nonlinearity.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.76 from 5 h onward, which suggests the reader has saturated. The retained 18 h aliquot supports this. Diluted 10x, it read 0.264 (replicates 0.261 and 0.267), which is about 2.64 once multiplied back. Diluted 30x, it read 0.090, which is about 2.71. A culture that was truly at 0.75 would read about 0.075 at 10x. The back-calculated value is also still creeping up with dilution (2.64 at 10x, 2.71 at 30x), so some compression remains at 10x. The true OD at 18 h is therefore about 2.7–2.8, roughly 3.5 times the undiluted reading.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.0974 at 10x dilution (three replicates, about 0.97 when corrected for dilution). At 3x dilution it read 0.320 (about 0.96 when corrected). The undiluted reading was 0.964. All three agree, so the reader responds proportionally in this range and is not saturating. If the plateau were an artefact of saturation, diluted samples would read higher than the undiluted reading once corrected. They don't. The plateau near 0.95 therefore looks like real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.3 from 7 h onward. This looks like reader saturation rather than a real stationary phase. The 18 h aliquot read 0.4777 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.4773 and 0.4780), which is about 4.78 after correcting for dilution. At 20x it read 0.2424, which is about 4.85. The two dilutions agree with each other, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. Both are about 3.7 times the undiluted reading of 1.32. The true late OD is therefore about 4.8, well above what the undiluted readings show.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.244 at 2-fold dilution (×2 = 0.488) and 0.0513 and 0.0506 at 10-fold dilution (×10 ≈ 0.51). The undiluted reading was 0.492. The dilution-corrected values match the undiluted reading, so the reader is responding linearly at OD ~0.5. If the plateau were reader saturation, diluted samples would read higher than 0.5 after correction. The plateau from 5 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.52 from 5 h onward. This looks like reader saturation, not stationary phase, because growth was exponential up to that point and then stopped abruptly at a fixed value. The 18 h aliquot read 0.193 at 10x dilution (×10 = 1.93) and 0.103 at 20x dilution (×20 = 2.06). Both are about four times the undiluted reading. The reader is linear at low OD: the 4 h aliquot read 0.144 at 2x dilution (×2 = 0.288), matching the undiluted 0.285. So the dilution results reflect real biomass and not a dilution artefact. The true 18 h OD is about 2.0–2.1, and the dilution-corrected value rises slightly with further dilution, which fits residual compression at 0.19.

The OD plateaus at about 0.43–0.45 from 5 h onward. I tested whether this was reader saturation by diluting the 18 h aliquot. At 3x dilution the readings were 0.149 and 0.156 (mean 0.1525), which is 0.457 after correcting for dilution. At 10x dilution the mean was 0.039 (0.043 and 0.035), which is 0.39 after correcting. Both are at or slightly below the undiluted reading of 0.443. If the undiluted reads were compressed by saturation, the dilution-corrected values would exceed the undiluted reading, and they do not. The plateau therefore looks like real stationary phase, and biomass at the final hours matches the undiluted readings.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 2.0 from 8 h onward, which looks like the reader saturating. Diluting the 18 h aliquot 10-fold gave 0.727 (replicates 0.724 and 0.729), which corresponds to about 7.3 OD undiluted. A 25-fold dilution gave 0.298, which corresponds to about 7.5. The two dilutions agree, so the diluted readings are in a proportional range. The true late OD is roughly 7.4, about 3.7 times the undiluted reading of 2.0.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.23 from 6 h onward. A plateau can be a true stationary phase or detector saturation, so I diluted the 18 h aliquot and scaled the readings back up. The 3x dilution gave 0.419, which is 1.26 OD. The 10x dilution gave 0.1325 and 0.1375, which is 1.35 OD. The 40x dilution gave 0.0276 and 0.0262, which is 1.08 OD. The undiluted reading was 1.21. The scaled values scatter around 1.2 with no monotonic rise as dilution increases. Saturation would make the scaled values climb with dilution. The replicate spread is about 4–5%, which accounts for the scatter. Reading and dilution agree, so biomass is as read, with an 18 h OD of about 1.2.

Undiluted readings plateau at about 1.85 from 9 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. Growth before that was exponential and doubled roughly every 1 h. The 18 h aliquot read 0.652 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.661 and 0.643), which corresponds to about 6.5 undiluted. At 25x it read 0.261, which corresponds to about 6.5 again. The two dilutions agree with each other, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The undiluted reading of 1.9 therefore underestimates the biomass by about 3.5-fold.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.73 from 7 h onward. I diluted retained aliquots to check whether the reader was saturating. At 18 h, a 3x dilution read 0.2435, which is 0.730 after correcting for dilution. Two 10x replicates read 0.0763 and 0.0770, which is about 0.766 after correcting. At 12 h, a 20x dilution read 0.0353, which is 0.706 after correcting. The undiluted 18 h reading was 0.728. All dilution-corrected values are within about 5% of the undiluted reading and show no systematic rise with dilution. If the reader were saturating, the corrected values would be well above the undiluted reading. The plateau therefore looks like real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.5 from 4 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. The 18 h aliquot read 0.193 at 10-fold dilution (replicates 0.189 and 0.198) and 0.0965 at 20-fold dilution. Both correct to about 1.93 OD, and the two dilutions agree, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The true 18 h biomass is about 4 times the undiluted reading of about 0.5.

I diluted the 18 h aliquot and scaled each reading back up by its dilution factor. The undiluted reading was 0.42, and the late-hour plateau averaged about 0.425. The 10-fold dilution gave 0.0432, which scales to 0.43. The 3-fold dilution gave 0.154, which scales to 0.46. The 2-fold dilution gave 0.227, which scales to 0.45. If the reader were saturating, the dilution-corrected values would sit well above the undiluted reading and rise as dilution increased. They sit only about 5% above it, which is within a couple of standard deviations of replicate noise (about ±0.005 absolute per read). The plateau from about 6 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase, not reader saturation. Any underestimate is small, at most roughly 5%.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.1 from 6 h onward, which suggests the reader is saturating. I read the 18 h aliquot after dilution. At 10x the mean was 0.523 (0.5275 and 0.5177), which corresponds to about 5.23 undiluted. At 40x the single reading was 0.129, which corresponds to about 5.17 undiluted. The two dilutions agree, so the diluted readings are in the linear range. The undiluted reading of about 1.1 is therefore compressed, and the true late biomass is about 5 times higher than it indicates.

I re-read the 18 h aliquot at three dilutions. Each reading was multiplied by its dilution factor to give an undiluted-equivalent OD. The 10x reads were 0.168 and 0.163, giving about 1.65. The 3x read was 0.538, giving about 1.61. The 30x read was 0.050, giving about 1.50. The undiluted reading was 1.55. All four estimates fall within about ±5% of each other and show no trend with dilution. If the reader were saturating at about 1.6, the diluted samples would have given much higher values. The plateau from about 7 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase. Biomass is at the level the readings indicate, perhaps 3–6% higher, which is within noise.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.93–0.95 from 5 h onward, which suggests reader saturation. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to test this. The 10x dilution read 0.361, which gives 3.6 when scaled. The 20x dilution read 0.170, which gives 3.4. The 50x dilution read 0.079, which gives 3.9. The scaled values are roughly consistent with each other, and the 50x value is the least affected by nonlinearity. Biomass at 18 h is therefore about 3.5–4 OD, roughly four times the undiluted reading of about 0.95. The plateau is a detector ceiling and not a real stationary phase at OD 0.93.

The 18 h aliquot was re-read at several dilutions. The readings, scaled back by the dilution factor, were 1.247 at 10x (mean of 2 replicates), 1.41 at 3x, 1.292 at 2x and 1.29 undiluted. All are about 1.3 with no upward trend as dilution increases. If the plateau were reader saturation, the diluted samples would read clearly higher than the undiluted one, and they don't. The 3x value is about 9% high, but the 2x value is not, so I treat it as noise. The plateau from 7 h onward therefore reflects true stationary phase, and biomass is at the level the readings indicate.

Undiluted readings plateau at ~0.9 from 6 h onward, which suggests the reader is saturating. A 10x dilution of the 18 h aliquot read 0.334 (n=3: 0.323, 0.334, 0.346). That is about 3.3 OD undiluted, roughly 3.7 times the undiluted reading of 0.91. A proportional reader would have given about 0.09 for that dilution. The 7 h aliquot at 10x read 0.239, which is about 2.4 OD undiluted against 0.91 read. So the culture kept growing after 6 h, and the flat undiluted readings reflect non-linear reader response at high density.

I diluted the retained 18 h aliquot and rescaled the readings by the dilution factor. If the reader were saturating, the rescaled values would rise above the undiluted 0.489. They didn't. The 10x dilution gave 0.0481, which scales to 0.481. The 4x dilution gave 0.1218 (two replicates, 0.1222 and 0.1214), which scales to 0.487. The single 2x reading gave 0.2613, which scales to 0.523. That is about 8% above the others and looks like a single-read outlier, since the 4x and 10x reads agree with the undiluted value. The plateau at about 0.48 from 5 h onward therefore reflects a real stationary phase, not a reader ceiling.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.65 from 7 h onward. Dilutions of the 18 h aliquot read much higher than 0.65 once scaled back up, so the reader is saturating. Scaled readings: 10x gave 0.251, or 2.51 equivalent. 40x gave 0.0552, or 2.21. 100x gave 0.0243, or 2.43. The scaled values are roughly consistent at about 2.2–2.5, and all are about 3.5 times the undiluted reading of 0.644. The 10x value may still be slightly compressed. The plateau therefore reflects reader non-linearity, not a stationary phase at that biomass.

I diluted retained aliquots and rescaled the readings by the dilution factor. The 18 h aliquot read 0.1201 at 10x (replicates 0.1185 and 0.1217), which scales to 1.20. At 3x it read 0.4024, which scales to 1.21. The 12 h aliquot read 0.1182 at 10x, which scales to 1.18. The undiluted readings for 12 to 18 h were 1.16 to 1.19. The diluted reads are therefore at most about 3% above the undiluted ones. That gap is comparable to the hour-to-hour scatter in the undiluted readings, which range from 1.10 to 1.19. A reader that saturates would give diluted readings well above the undiluted plateau, and I saw no such gap. The plateau therefore appears to be a real stationary phase at an OD600 of about 1.2.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.2 from 7 h onward. The plateau is flat and noisy, which suggests the reader is saturating. The retained 18 h aliquot read 0.482 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.479 and 0.484), which is 4.82 after correcting for dilution. At 40x it read 0.123, which is 4.92 after correcting. The two dilutions agree with each other, so the reader is roughly linear in this range. The undiluted reading of about 1.2 is therefore compressed. The true 18 h OD is about 4.9, roughly four times the undiluted reading.

The 18 h aliquot read 0.0953 at 10x dilution (two replicates, 0.094 and 0.0967), which scales to 0.953. At 3x dilution it read 0.3127, which scales to 0.938. The undiluted reading was 0.9625. All three agree within noise, so the reader responds proportionally and is not saturating. If it were saturating, the diluted readings would scale to values clearly above 0.96. The plateau at about 0.96 from 6 h onward therefore reflects real stationary-phase biomass.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.93–0.97 from 6 h onward, which looks like detector saturation. Dilutions of the 18 h aliquot do not scale back to that value. The 10x dilution read 0.478 (replicates 0.481 and 0.475), which is 4.78 when multiplied back. The 25x dilution read 0.182 (4.56 corrected). The 50x dilution read 0.091 (4.57 corrected). The 25x and 50x corrected values agree at about 4.6, which suggests the reader is linear at those readings. The 10x value is slightly higher, so it may also carry some saturation. The true OD at 18 h is therefore about 4.6, roughly 5 times the undiluted reading of 0.92, so the plateau is a reader ceiling rather than the biomass level.

The OD plateaus at about 0.53 from 5 h to 18 h. A plateau like this could be detector saturation hiding continued growth, so I diluted the 18 h aliquot to test it. Dilution-corrected readings were: x2 gave 0.537, x5 gave 0.515, x10 gave 0.575 (two replicates), and x25 gave 0.61 (two replicates, noisy). The undiluted reading was 0.531. If the reader were saturating, the corrected values would rise steadily with dilution and sit well above 0.53. Here the x2 and x5 values match the undiluted reading, and the x10 and x25 values are only modestly higher and noisy. They are not a monotonic trend, since x5 is lower than x2. The x10 and x25 values fit replicate scatter at low OD, where the replicates differed by roughly 7–25%. The reader looks linear up to about 0.53, so the plateau is a real stationary phase.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.67 from 7 h onward. The 18 h aliquot read 0.33 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.337 and 0.324), which corresponds to about 3.3 undiluted. At 20x it read 0.161, which corresponds to about 3.2. The two dilutions agree with each other, and both are roughly 5 times the undiluted reading. The plateau therefore comes from the reader saturating at high density, not from growth stopping. The true OD at 18 h is about 3.2–3.3.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.60–0.65 from hour 5 onward. I diluted the 18 h aliquot to test whether the reader was saturating. If it were, diluted readings multiplied by the dilution factor would come out clearly above 0.60, and more so at higher dilution. They didn't. Undiluted was 0.605. At 3x the two replicates gave 0.2031 and 0.2032, which scale to 0.609. At 10x the mean was 0.0652, which scales to 0.652. At 30x the mean was 0.0188, which scales to 0.564, though the two replicates were noisy (0.0212 and 0.0165). The scaled values scatter around 0.6 with no upward trend as dilution increases, so the reader responds proportionally in this range. The plateau therefore reflects a real stationary phase, and the biomass is as read.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 1.1 from 9 h onward, which could be reader saturation. The retained 18 h aliquot read 0.520 at 10x dilution (replicates 0.5245 and 0.5157) and 0.2575 at 20x. That gives about 5.2 and 5.15 after correcting for dilution, which agree with each other. If the undiluted reading of 1.10 were proportional, the 10x dilution would read about 0.11. The reader therefore saturates at high density, and the true late biomass is roughly 5 times what the undiluted readings show. The apparent stationary phase is a plateau in the reading only.

The 18 h aliquot was read at three dilutions, and the dilution-corrected values are about the same as the undiluted reading. The undiluted reading was 1.34. The ×10 reading (two replicates) corrected to 1.47, the ×20 reading (two replicates) to 1.33, and the ×40 reading (one replicate) to 1.40. Only the ×10 value is clearly higher. The ×20 value matches the undiluted reading. The mean of the three, about 1.40, is roughly 4% above 1.34, which is within the scatter between dilutions. If the reader were saturating, the corrected values would rise steadily with dilution, and they do not. The 6 h aliquot, read ×10, corrected to 0.99 against 0.93 undiluted, which is mild, and the reading is not near the plateau. The flat plateau at about 1.35 from 7 h onward therefore looks like real stationary phase and not a hidden increase in biomass. I did not detect a significant undercount. The remaining uncertainty is the ×10 result and the small budget, which left only single replicates at some dilutions.

The undiluted readings plateau at about 0.65 from 5 h onward, right after exponential growth. That pattern fits detector saturation. I read the 18 h aliquot after dilution. At 10x it gave 0.3015 (replicates 0.3075 and 0.2955), which corresponds to about 3.0 undiluted. At 40x it gave 0.077, which corresponds to about 3.1. Both dilutions agree on roughly 3, about 4.7 times the undiluted reading of 0.65. If the plateau were real biomass, the dilutions would have given about 0.065 and 0.016. The reader is therefore non-linear at high density, and the true late biomass is about 3.1 OD-equivalent.
